note: Standard spelling is التي, not التى.
proposed_target: هناك بعض الأشياء التي من الصعب ترجمتها.
proposed_english: There are some things that are difficult to translate.

note: English explicitly says people; make the Arabic equally explicit.
proposed_target: كان هناك ثلاثة أشخاص ينتظرون أمامي.
proposed_english: There were three people waiting in front of me.

note: Missing hamza in أستطع.
proposed_target: لسوء الحظ، كنت مشغولًا بالأمس ولم أستطع فعل ذلك.
proposed_english: Unfortunately, I was busy yesterday and couldn't do that.

note: ثلاثة من الكناري is awkward; use ثلاثة طيور كناري.
proposed_target: عندنا كلب وقط وثلاثة طيور كناري.
proposed_english: We have a dog, a cat and three canaries.

note: After لم use نرَ, not نرى; English is also missing 'of' in 'a lot of tourists'.
proposed_target: لم نرَ الكثير من السياح بالقرب من هنا مؤخرًا.
proposed_english: We haven't seen a lot of tourists around here lately.

note: Arabic says very expensive, not necessarily too expensive.
proposed_target: كلما وجدت شيئًا يعجبني، وجدته غاليًا جدًا.
proposed_english: Whenever I find something I like, it's very expensive.

note: Verb is يبدو, not يبدوا.
proposed_target: لا يبدو أنك تعرف ما سيحصل.
proposed_english: You don't seem to know what's going to happen.

note: Current ما كان عليك فعله can read as 'what you had to do'; intended meaning is something you should not have done.
proposed_target: تبدو وكأنك فعلت شيئًا لم يكن عليك فعله.
proposed_english: You look like you've been doing something you shouldn't.

note: Arabic means 'we will follow you'; use an uncontracted natural equivalent that remains in the audited C-band.
proposed_target: أيها الناس، امضوا قدمًا. سنتبعكم.
proposed_english: You people go on ahead. We will follow you.

note: English adds 'please', absent from Arabic.
proposed_target: أيمكنك أن تخبرني متى يغادر القطار؟
proposed_english: Can you tell me what time the train leaves?

note: Use an explicit natural help request in both languages while preserving the audited C-band.
proposed_target: هل يمكنك أن تقدم لي بعض المساعدة في المطبخ؟
proposed_english: Can you give me some help in the kitchen?

note: تعلّمني means teach me, not tell me; Arabic has the washing machine, not explicitly 'this'.
proposed_target: أيمكنك أن تعلّمني كيف أستخدم الغسّالة؟
proposed_english: Could you teach me how to use the washing machine?

note: الأن is misspelled; correct form is الآن.
proposed_target: هل تريدني حقًا أن أذهب إلى هناك الآن؟
proposed_english: Do you really want me to go there right now?

note: English adds the intensifier 'so', absent from Arabic.
proposed_target: لماذا خلدت للنوم مبكرًا الليلة الماضية؟
proposed_english: Why did you go to sleep early last night?

note: الأولاد means boys; English 'guys' is broader/colloquial.
proposed_target: لماذا تهتم البنات بما يفكّر الأولاد لهذه الدرجة؟
proposed_english: Why do girls care so much about what boys think?

note: Arabic is direct 'Do you want'; English uses softer 'Would you like'.
proposed_target: هل تريد أن تذهب إلى حديقة الحيوان بعد ظهر هذا اليوم؟
proposed_english: Do you want to go to the zoo this afternoon?

note: Missing hamzas in أعتقد أننا.
proposed_target: لا أعتقد أننا نملك الوقت الكافي لفعل ذلك.
proposed_english: I don't think we have enough time to do that.

note: Current بين و بينك is malformed and omits the first party; use بيني وبينك.
proposed_target: لا أريد أن تكون بيني وبينك أي صلة.
proposed_english: I don't want to have anything to do with you.

note: Bare لم is ambiguous for why; use لماذا.
proposed_target: أريد أن أعرف لماذا كنت مضطرًا للقيام بذلك.
proposed_english: I want to know why I needed to do that.

note: Arabic past لم يؤذن لي means 'I wasn't allowed'; English present 'I'm not allowed' mismatches tense.
proposed_target: لم يؤذن لي بإطلاعك على ما تريد معرفته.
proposed_english: I wasn't allowed to tell you what you want to know.

note: Question punctuation is wrong, الشيء is misspelled, and the conditional is better expressed directly.
proposed_target: لو كنت مكانك، لفعلت الشيء نفسه.
proposed_english: If I were you, I would do the same.

note: Express the idiom 'the decision is in your hands' as the natural equivalent 'it is up to you to make the decision', preserving C-band progression.
proposed_target: الأمر متروك لك الآن لاتخاذ القرار.
proposed_english: It is up to you to make the decision now.

note: Normalize عليّ and learner-facing wording.
proposed_target: أخبرني الطبيب أن عليّ شرب المزيد من الماء.
proposed_english: My doctor told me that I should drink more water.
